CONTEXT: I need a TIMED SPRINT DPP for [CLASS/GRADE] students preparing for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / JEE / NEET / State Board]. Topic = [TOPIC]. Total time allowed = [TOTAL TIME e.g. 12 minutes].

YOUR TASK:
1. Create exactly 8 fast, clean questions on [TOPIC] that a strong student can do mostly mentally or in a few lines.
2. Assign a target time in seconds to each question so the totals add up to the total time allowed.
3. Build in a difficulty curve: quick early wins, two tougher ones near the end.
4. Give hints, an answer key, and a speed-tips note.

INPUT: Topic = [TOPIC]. Class = [CLASS/GRADE]. Board/Exam = [BOARD or EXAM]. Total time = [TOTAL TIME]. If unclear, assume and state it in one line.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve each question yourself first and time how few steps it really needs. Verify every final answer by two independent checks. Pick only questions with quick, clean answers - avoid heavy calculation. Never invent formulas or values. Keep all maths legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text.

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this exact order:
1. TITLE BLOCK: 'Sprint DPP - [TOPIC] - Total time [TOTAL TIME]' with class, board/exam, and 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
2. PACE PLAN: a small table of question number and target seconds, with the total.
3. SECTION A - QUESTIONS: the 8 numbered questions only, printable.
4. SECTION B - HINTS: one one-line hint per question.
5. SECTION C - ANSWER KEY: final answers.
6. SECTION D - SPEED TIPS: three short tips for going faster on this topic.

RULES: Keep each question genuinely fast. The per-question seconds must sum exactly to the total time. No long multi-page problems.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematics teacher who opens every class with a short confidence-building warm-up.

CONTEXT: I want a quick MORNING WARM-UP of 5 short questions to start the day or lesson for [CLASS/GRADE] students of [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. Topic = [TOPIC or 'mixed easy revision']. Total time = about 5 minutes.

YOUR TASK:
1. Create exactly 5 short, mostly mental or one-line questions that a student can finish in about a minute each.
2. Keep them encouraging: easy enough to build momentum, with maybe one slightly thoughtful one at the end.
3. Provide instant one-line answers and a single 'thought for the day' style maths fact.

INPUT: Topic = [TOPIC]. Class = [CLASS/GRADE]. Board/Exam = [BOARD or EXAM]. If unclear, assume and state it.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve each question yourself first and confirm it is truly quick. Verify each final answer by two independent checks. Avoid heavy calculation. Never invent formulas or values. Keep all maths legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text.

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this exact order:
1. TITLE LINE: 'Morning Warm-Up - [TOPIC]' with class and 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
2. QUESTIONS: 5 short numbered questions, printable.
3. QUICK ANSWERS: the 5 final answers in one tidy list.
4. MATHS SPARK: one short, interesting one-line maths fact tied to the topic to spark curiosity.

RULES: Keep it short and uplifting. Nothing here should take more than a minute. No multi-page problems.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
